readout_other: Cross-modal video-word associative memory task (cued recall accuracy and retrieval reaction time); side-effects questionnaire
direction_notes: U-taVNS did not significantly improve associative memory accuracy versus sham or pre-stimulation, and unlike E-taVNS, did not produce a hastening of reaction times for correctly recalled items (active vs sham hastening for E-taVNS: t(29)=-2.999, p=0.003; no equivalent effect for U-taVNS: t(27)=-0.391, p=0.349).
safety_notes: No significant aversive effects were observed relative to sham in either modality, though skin irritation was more frequently reported with E-taVNS than U-taVNS (chi2=3.86, p=0.049), indicating U-taVNS was associated with a lower incidence of skin irritation than E-taVNS. Minor events (e.g. dizziness, ear pain, other) were reported by a small number of U-taVNS participants (Table 2).

exposures.label: Ultrasound taVNS (U-taVNS) to right cymba conchae

timing.protocol_description: Participants received 30 minutes of taVNS per session; each participant completed two sessions (active and sham), scheduled >=5 days apart, with stimulation order counterbalanced. For the sham condition, a dedicated sham device reproduced the same auditory buzzing sound as the active device but delivered no ultrasound output, matching auditory cues between active and sham sessions.

source_quotes.n_subjects: A total of 59 healthy adults (46 women, 13 men; mean = 23.6 years, SD = 2.88) participated in the study. Participants were randomly allocated to either the electrical stimulation group (EtaVNS; n = 30) or the ultrasound stimulation group (U-taVNS; n = 29).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Each participant completed two sessions (active and sham), scheduled ≥five days apart, with stimulation order counterbalanced across participants.
source_quotes.randomised: A total of 59 healthy adults (46 women, 13 men; mean = 23.6 years, SD = 2.88) participated in the study. Participants were randomly allocated to either the electrical stimulation group (EtaVNS; n = 30) or the ultrasound stimulation group (U-taVNS; n = 29).
source_quotes.blinding: Participants were informed that two different stimulation protocols would be tested but were not told which session involved sham stimulation. At the end of the second session, participants were verbally asked whether they could distinguish between the two conditions. No participant reported being able to identify the active stimulation session, suggesting that the blinding procedure was effective.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: For U-taVNS, stimulation was applied to the right cymba conchae. The ultrasound protocol used a center frequency of 5.3 MHz, a pulse repetition frequency of 41 Hz, a 50% duty cycle, a peak mechanical output of 0.081 ${ \mathsf { W } } / { \mathsf { c m } } ^ { 2 } ,$ and an average pressure amplitude of 1.03 MPa. For the U-taVNS sham condition, a dedicated sham device was used that reproduced the same auditory buzzing sound as the active device but delivered no ultrasound output. This ensured that auditory cues associated with device operation were matched between active and sham sessions.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: After the first completion of the task, participants received 30 minutes of taVNS. Immediately after stimulation, they completed the associative memory task again in the poststimulation phase.
source_quotes.direction_notes: We did not, however, observe any effects of U-taVNS on associative memory performance. This null result should be interpreted with caution owing to two key differences between our ultrasound and electrical protocols.
source_quotes.safety_notes: no significant aversive effects were observed relative to sham in either modality. However, skin irritation was more frequently reported in the eVNS group than in the uVNS group, yielding a significant association between stimulation type and skin irritation (χ<sup>2</sup> = 3.86, p = 0.049). This finding indicates that U-taVNS was associated with a lower incidence of skin irritation than was EtaVNS.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: taVNS was delivered using two modalities: electrical stimulation (Healaon Pro, Neurive Inc, Gimhae, Republic of Korea) and ultrasound stimulation (ZenBud, NeurGear Inc, Rochester, NY).

flags.reason: The paper reports this as 'an average pressure amplitude of 1.03 MPa', which is unambiguously a pressure value; converted to 1030 kPa.
'A peak mechanical output of 0.081 W/cm2' is not explicitly labelled ISPPA or ISPTA; assigned to ISPPA given the word 'peak', but this is an inference.
Duty cycle (50%) and PRF (41 Hz) are stated but pulse duration is not; not computed per the no-arithmetic rule.
The paper does not state whether the reported pressure/intensity values are free-field or in-situ; recorded under unspecified_domain.
The U-taVNS sham used a separate 'dedicated sham device' rather than the active transducer powered off; classified as inactive_transducer (no acoustic output) as the closest vocabulary match.
